item.title: Koyasan Candle Festival: 100,000 Lights Along Okunoin — Guide
item.description: The Koyasan Candle Festival (Rosoku Matsuri), held on the evening of August 13th at the start of Obon, is one of Japan’s most moving summer sights. Along the entire two-kilometre approach to Okunoin, from Ichinohashi bridge to Kobo Daishi’s mausoleum, some 100,000 candles are set out and lit by visitors and pilgrims, so that the path through the ancient cedars becomes a shimmering river of small flames winding between 200,000 tombs.

item.title: Okunoin: Japan's Largest Cemetery Beneath the Cedars — Guide
item.description: Okunoin is the spiritual climax of Koyasan and the largest cemetery in Japan: a two-kilometre path winding beneath towering, centuries-old cedars past some 200,000 tombstones, memorials and mossy stupas, from feudal lords and famous samurai to company memorials and modern graves. At its far end stands the Gobyo, the mausoleum of Kobo Daishi, who is believed by the faithful not to have died but to rest in eternal meditation, awaiting the future Buddha — monks still carry him meals twice daily.
